This is a project-sized piece of work, so I'll write it as a full design document and save it in the museum's repository under `specs/`. A reviewer will read it before you do, and I may come back once with a few questions.

Before I write it, I need to settle one choice about how it's built, and ask you one thing.

**Where uploads go.** Your website is a set of fixed pages hosted on Netlify. It has nothing that can accept a file or clean up audio, so the guide needs that added. There are two reasonable ways:

1. **Build it into the existing website.** Volunteers log in to a simple editing page, pick an exhibit and a language, and upload their recording. The site rebuilds itself, cleans up the audio as part of that rebuild, and publishes a guide page for each exhibit. The codes point to those pages. This keeps everything in what you already run, and the recordings are saved with full history. The downside is that each upload takes a few minutes to go live.
2. **Run a separate small upload service on Netlify.** Recordings go live within seconds and don't require a rebuild. The downside is more custom code that someone has to look after.

I'll go with (1). Ten uploads a year doesn't justify the extra code, and volunteers need to log in either way so that strangers can't upload. Tell me if you'd rather have the other.

**One question.** What's prompting the audio guide now, and what would make you say it worked a year from now? Your answer sets what the design counts as success and what it treats as a failure, even if everything technically runs.
